title: Use Scratchpad as the working name
decision: Use Scratchpad as the working product name.
rationale: The user selected the name during the referenced product discussion.

title: Enough direction to begin specification and a first vertical slice
finding: Available product choices are sufficient to begin a PRD and initial architecture. Record/API semantics, first-owner enrollment, project identity rules, and acceptance criteria require specification before their dependent implementation.
evidence: Conversation reader returned the final five exchanges with no older-page cursor. Workspace initially contained only Git metadata and no commits.
limitations: Original user approval of every stack choice was not visible; those choices appear in the prior assistant summary. No application implementation, current dependency validation, or deployment occurred.

title: Author the PRD in the Scratchpad repository
decision: Create and maintain docs/prd.md as the repository product specification, using the original discovery conversation as a source.
rationale: Keep the specification versionable and available to future project sessions.
limitations: The instruction authorizes authoring; new requirements and stage boundaries remain draft proposals unless separately supported by explicit user choices.

title: Treat JSONL as bootstrap memory with an intended Scratchpad successor

source.quote: decision.jsonl will be obsolete when this project is done hopefully

decision: Aim to use Scratchpad for its own project memory rather than require permanent hand-maintained JSONL capture.
rationale: The product should fulfill the memory role currently served by the bootstrap log.
proposed_acceptance: Import the bootstrap log, demonstrate capture and retrieval from a fresh session, and validate export/recovery before an explicit owner switch. Repository mirroring remains optional.
limitations: The reliability gate is a PRD proposal; no migration or switch has occurred.

title: PRD v0.1 separates recovered decisions from proposed implementation scope
finding: The draft defines an implementation-contract stage, a first capture/retrieval slice, a useful V1, and later optional analysis/backend work. It includes a single-owner proposal, testable acceptance scenarios, and open gates for authentication, record semantics, project identity, credential permissions, mirroring, and raw-data removal policy.
rationale: Make implementation reviewable while preserving provenance and uncertainty in the recovered discovery context.
limitations: Draft authorship does not approve every new default, verify technology compatibility, or establish implementation and release acceptance.

title: Development start needs concrete contracts and workspace identity rules

source.request: let's see what's missing for a good development start

finding: The workspace contains only planning documents. Foundation work can begin; dependent implementation needs owner scope, enrollment/deployment assumptions, concrete record/API/MCP contracts, active workspace resolution, and reproducible scaffold/acceptance checks. PRD ambiguities include analysis-versus-retrieval eligibility, mirror coverage and acceptance semantics, and exact M1 requirements.
recommendation: Resolve owner scope first, then deployment/auth expectations; write architecture and first-slice contracts, clarify the PRD, and scaffold with executable acceptance checks. Defer optional analysis and later-release questions.
limitations: Recommendations are not adopted decisions. No stack compatibility validation, remote repository inspection, implementation, commit, or deployment occurred.

title: Original user-supplied PRD replaces incomplete reconstruction
finding: Original PRD closes owner scope, stack, deployment shape, tool shape, release targets, and owner-authorized raw-removal direction. Restores business-decision mirroring, restart-safe authentication state, native search filters, signed/notarized macOS artifacts, and full MVP scope.

supersedes.scope: Canonical PRD reconstruction and proposed milestone authority
Claims that owner, core stack, deployment shape and distribution targets remain unspecified; reconstruction-specific mirror/search assumptions

limitations: Supplied product direction is not proof of dependency compatibility or implementation. Prior draft engineering proposals remain proposals. Current-session self-dogfooding intent remains applicable.

title: User-supplied architecture and API establish implementation baseline
finding: Saved both source documents verbatim. Architecture and conceptual API are no longer missing. Record vocabularies, payloads, persistence concepts, endpoint subset, repository layout recommendation, and SQLite-first implementation sequence are specified.

supersedes.scope: Need to author architecture and conceptual data/API contract from scratch; those documents are now supplied

remaining_work: Trusted enrollment and exact challenge/token behavior
Complete payload/project-create schemas and server-derived attribution
Dependency validation, scaffold and executable acceptance checks
limitations: Suggested options remain suggestions. No application implementation, compatibility verification, commit, or deployment occurred.

title: Checkpoint initial documentation before implementation decisions

source.quote: let's commit this state with intial docs then let's answer the questions with ur recommendations

decision: Create a local initial documentation commit, then discuss recommended resolutions to remaining implementation details.
limitations: Commit request does not authorize a push or adopt subsequent recommendations.

title: Browser-first enrollment and administrator-controlled recovery

source.quote: Yeah no headaches identified, it's a clean pattern

decision: Use a short-lived single-use setup token generated by an administrator command in the container to enroll the first browser passkey; use SimpleWebAuthn. Manage additional passkeys and MCP public keys through the authenticated dashboard, requiring MCP proof of possession. Disable ordinary setup after enrollment. Recover access through a separate audited administrator-authorized replacement-passkey flow that preserves project data.
rationale: Simple passwordless setup with server administrative access as the recovery authority, without email or an external identity provider.
limitations: No authentication implementation exists yet. Exact command/endpoint names, lifetimes, MCP signing format, and recovery session handling remain to be specified.

title: Keep MCP authentication simple with day-long sessions
decision: Authenticate with a random short-lived single-use signed challenge and issue a session valid up to 24 hours. Keep the client token in MCP process memory, authenticate again after MCP restart or expiry, invalidate sessions immediately on credential revocation, and omit refresh tokens.
rationale: Avoid repeated signing prompts and unnecessary authentication complexity.
limitations: Exact signature fields/format, challenge TTL, and server token representation remain engineering details; the earlier 15-minute session and two-minute challenge suggestions are not adopted requirements. Server-side session state remains restart-safe.

title: Default MCP discovery to launch directory with per-call override
decision: Use MCP process launch directory for project discovery by default. Accept optional workingDirectory on project-scoped calls when the agent works elsewhere; keep overrides local to each call. Include resolved project in results and preserve existing ambiguity handling.
rationale: Keep the usual project-launched stdio workflow automatic while accommodating globally launched or reused MCP servers.
limitations: This does not imply stdio guarantees a project working directory or authorize central-server filesystem access. The earlier mandatory-directory proposal was not adopted.

title: Use flexible typed payloads without duplicate authored content

source.quote: yes but keep in mind we need to keep this flexible and adapt it while we use

decision: Capture natural type-specific fields once into immutable payloads; derive readable content deterministically. Server supplies IDs, receipt timestamps and verified credential attribution. Create records using resolved projectId for Git and non-Git projects. Keep schemas lightweight and adaptable through usage, preserving original captures and historical readability as shapes evolve.
rationale: Avoid duplicate agent-authored text without prematurely freezing the model.
limitations: Exact schema versioning, compatibility and rendering mechanics remain implementation details. Imported original content must still be preserved; no dynamic schema engine or rigid comprehensive taxonomy is required.

title: Replay capture retries and reject stale edits without automatic merging
decision: Return the existing record when the same capture request is retried. Return a conflict for changed content under the same request identity or an edit based on a stale revision. Preserve separate intentional captures even when text matches. Do not automatically merge or deduplicate by content.
rationale: Predictable retry and concurrency behavior with minimal complexity.
limitations: Key scope, payload comparison, retention, and concurrency wire representation remain implementation details.

title: Keep repository mirroring local, central-first and optional
decision: Mirror eligible MCP captures only when both local configuration and project settings permit. Persist centrally first, append locally second, report mirror failure separately, and retry without duplicate central or mirrored records. Default eligible types are decision, adr and business_decision. No browser-to-repository synchronization or automatic Git commit/push.
rationale: A simple optional dual-write workflow is sufficient for initial development.
limitations: Exact mirror-result API and concurrent append/retry mechanics remain implementation details.
